1	# Registro de prompts (ad-hoc)
2	
3	Registro mantido pelo pesquisador com os prompts livres enviados nesta execução, na ordem de envio.
4	
5	## Prompt 1 (inicial)
6	
7	- Horário:
8	- Texto enviado (copiar o bloco abaixo sem alterações):
9	
10	````markdown
11	# Recorte A da API Conduit (RealWorld)
12	
13	## Objetivo
14	
15	Implementar o backend do recorte A da API Conduit, uma plataforma de publicação de artigos no estilo do Medium. O recorte cobre:
16	
17	- autenticação de usuários via JWT: cadastro e login;
18	- consulta e atualização do usuário autenticado (não há exclusão de usuário);
19	- consulta do perfil público de um usuário;
20	- seguir e deixar de seguir outros usuários.
21	
22	Os demais recursos da API Conduit (artigos, feed, comentários, favoritos e tags) estão fora do escopo.
23	
24	## Contrato da API
25	
26	O contrato abaixo é obrigatório: rotas, formatos JSON, códigos de status e formato de erro. Se a descrição em prosa divergir da especificação OpenAPI, vale a especificação OpenAPI.
27	
28	### Endpoints
29	
30	
31	#### Authentication Header:
32	
33	You can read the authentication header from the headers of the request
34	
35	`Authorization: Token jwt.token.here`
36	
37	#### Authentication:
38	
39	`POST /api/users/login`
40	
41	Example request body:
42	
43	```json
44	{
45	  "user":{
46	    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
47	    "password": "jakejake"
48	  }
49	}
50	```
51	
52	No authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication)
53	
54	Required fields: `email`, `password`
55	
56	#### Registration:
57	
58	`POST /api/users`
59	
60	Example request body:
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "user":{
65	    "username": "Jacob",
66	    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
67	    "password": "jakejake"
68	  }
69	}
70	```
71	
72	No authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication)
73	
74	Required fields: `email`, `username`, `password`
75	
76	#### Get Current User
77	
78	`GET /api/user`
79	
80	Authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication) that's the current user
81	
82	#### Update User
83	
84	`PUT /api/user`
85	
86	Example request body:
87	
88	```json
89	{
90	  "user":{
91	    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
92	    "bio": "I like to skateboard",
93	    "image": "https://i.stack.imgur.com/xHWG8.jpg"
94	  }
95	}
96	```
97	
98	Authentication required, returns the [User](#users-for-authentication)
99	
100	Accepted fields: `email`, `username`, `password`, `image`, `bio`
101	
102	#### Get Profile
103	
104	`GET /api/profiles/:username`
105	
106	Authentication optional, returns a [Profile](#profile)
107	
108	#### Follow user
109	
110	`POST /api/profiles/:username/follow`
111	
112	Authentication required, returns a [Profile](#profile)
113	
114	No additional parameters required
115	
116	#### Unfollow user
117	
118	`DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow`
119	
120	Authentication required, returns a [Profile](#profile)
121	
122	No additional parameters required
123	
124	
125	### Formato das respostas
126	
127	Make sure the right content type like `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` is correctly returned.
128	
129	#### Users (for authentication)
130	
131	```json
132	{
133	  "user": {
134	    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
135	    "token": "jwt.token.here",
136	    "username": "jake",
137	    "bio": null,
138	    "image": null
139	  }
140	}
141	```
142	
143	#### Profile
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "profile": {
148	    "username": "jake",
149	    "bio": "I work at statefarm",
150	    "image": "https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpg",
151	    "following": false
152	  }
153	}
154	```
155	
156	
157	### Erros
158	
159	If a request fails any validations, expect a 422 and errors in the following format:
160	
161	```json
162	{
163	  "errors":{
164	    "body": [
165	      "can't be empty"
166	    ]
167	  }
168	}
169	```
170	
171	#### Other status codes:
172	
173	401 for Unauthorized requests, when a request requires authentication but it isn't provided
174	
175	403 for Forbidden requests, when a request may be valid but the user doesn't have permissions to perform the action
176	
177	404 for Not found requests, when a resource can't be found to fulfill the request
178	
179	### Especificação OpenAPI

# Registro de prompts (ad-hoc)

Registro mantido pelo pesquisador com os prompts livres enviados nesta execução, na ordem de envio.

## Prompt 1 (inicial)

````markdown
# Recorte A da API Conduit (RealWorld)

## Objetivo

Implementar o backend do recorte A da API Conduit, uma plataforma de publicação de artigos no estilo do Medium. O recorte cobre:

- autenticação de usuários via JWT: cadastro e login;
- consulta e atualização do usuário autenticado (não há exclusão de usuário);
- consulta do perfil público de um usuário;
- seguir e deixar de seguir outros usuários.

Os demais recursos da API Conduit (artigos, feed, comentários, favoritos e tags) estão fora do escopo.

## Contrato da API

O contrato abaixo é obrigatório: rotas, formatos JSON, códigos de status e formato de erro. Se a descrição em prosa divergir da especificação OpenAPI, vale a especificação OpenAPI.

### Endpoints


#### Authentication Header:

You can read the authentication header from the headers of the request

`Authorization: Token jwt.token.here`

#### Authentication:

`POST /api/users/login`

Example request body:

```json
{
  "user":{
    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
    "password": "jakejake"
  }
}
```

No authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication)

Required fields: `email`, `password`

#### Registration:

`POST /api/users`

Example request body:

```json
{
  "user":{
    "username": "Jacob",
    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
    "password": "jakejake"
  }
}
```

No authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication)

Required fields: `email`, `username`, `password`

#### Get Current User

`GET /api/user`

Authentication required, returns a [User](#users-for-authentication) that's the current user

#### Update User

`PUT /api/user`

Example request body:

```json
{
  "user":{
    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
    "bio": "I like to skateboard",
    "image": "https://i.stack.imgur.com/xHWG8.jpg"
  }
}
```

Authentication required, returns the [User](#users-for-authentication)

Accepted fields: `email`, `username`, `password`, `image`, `bio`

#### Get Profile

`GET /api/profiles/:username`

Authentication optional, returns a [Profile](#profile)

#### Follow user

`POST /api/profiles/:username/follow`

Authentication required, returns a [Profile](#profile)

No additional parameters required

#### Unfollow user

`DELETE /api/profiles/:username/follow`

Authentication required, returns a [Profile](#profile)

No additional parameters required


### Formato das respostas

Make sure the right content type like `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` is correctly returned.

#### Users (for authentication)

```json
{
  "user": {
    "email": "jake@jake.jake",
    "token": "jwt.token.here",
    "username": "jake",
    "bio": null,
    "image": null
  }
}
```

#### Profile

```json
{
  "profile": {
    "username": "jake",
    "bio": "I work at statefarm",
    "image": "https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpg",
    "following": false
  }
}
```


### Erros

If a request fails any validations, expect a 422 and errors in the following format:

```json
{
  "errors":{
    "body": [
      "can't be empty"
    ]
  }
}
```

#### Other status codes:

401 for Unauthorized requests, when a request requires authentication but it isn't provided

403 for Forbidden requests, when a request may be valid but the user doesn't have permissions to perform the action

404 for Not found requests, when a resource can't be found to fulfill the request
````

I fixed all 8 failures, but I couldn't run the Hurl suite itself because the `.hurl` files aren't in this repository. I worked from your error output and the OpenAPI contract instead. `./mvnw verify` passes: 38 tests, none failing.

**1. `PUT /api/user` with `bio: null` or `image: null` (auth.hurl lines 120–244)**
The contract allows `null` for `bio` and `image`, and the suite expects it to clear the value. The API was treating `null` as "field not sent", so a body like `{"user":{"bio":null}}` was rejected with 422 because it looked empty.
- `UpdateUserRequest.Changes` is now a class that records which fields the client actually sent, so it can tell a missing field from an explicit `null`.
- An explicit `null` (or an empty string) in `bio` or `image` now clears the value.
- A missing field is still left unchanged.

**2. `PUT /api/user` returned 200 instead of 422 (errors_auth.hurl:204)**
In the contract, `email`, `username` and `password` are plain strings that can't be `null`. An explicit `null` in any of them now returns 422 with `{"errors":{"email":["can't be blank"]}}` (or the matching field name). This is my best guess at what that request sends, since I can't see the file. If line 204 sends something else, tell me the body and I'll adjust.

**3. Login error format (errors_auth.hurl:113)**
Wrong credentials still return 401, but the body is now `{"errors":{"credentials":["invalid"]}}` instead of `{"errors":{"email or password":["is invalid"]}}`. The change is in `UserService.java:71`.

The changed files are `UpdateUserRequest.java`, `UserController.java`, `UserService.java` and `ConduitApiIT.java`. In `ConduitApiIT.java` I updated the login test to the new format and added tests for clearing with `null` and for rejecting a `null` email.

Please run the Hurl suite again to confirm.
